recipes.name: Harvest Pork Stew
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds boneless pork, cut into 1/2-inch cubes

steps.text: Melt butter in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add pork; cook until lightly browned on all sides. Stir in onion and garlic; cook until onion softens and pork is no longer pink, about 5 minutes.
Add chicken broth, bay leaf, salt, rosemary, and sage; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Cover pot; simmer for 20 minutes.
Add squash, apples, potatoes, and carrots; return to a simmer. Cook, uncovered, until squash and apples are tender, about 20 minutes. Remove and discard bay leaf.

raw_recipe.headline: Harvest Pork Stew
raw_recipe.description: This harvest pork stew recipe gets its savory-sweet notes from butternut squash and apples. This stew can be made on the stovetop or in a slow cooker.

review.reviewBody: Excellent! I made this tonight in my slow cooker with the pork chunks, red potatoes, onions, baby carrots, and apple (didn't have the squash). It turned out super tender and SO tasty.

Big hit with the family! It was like having a breath of Autumn in the middle of a hot, humid Florida August! I made this in a crockpot, because I love slow cooking, and smelling this cook all day in the house was amazing! I made a few changes, mostly because of what I had on-hand, and my family's preferences. I used 2 Yukon Gold potatoes, I cup carrots, 1 cup parsnips (my husband loves them), I small sweet onion, garlic, I was lucky to have frozen butternut squash in the freezer, and I had 2 Ambrosia apples. I upped the spices considerably. I probably doubled or even tripled the sage and the rosemary. I also added white pepper. I used all 3 cups of chicken broth. I started the recipe off by dusting the pork with salt, pepper, and flour, and browning the meat in a little olive oil. After removing the meat, I threw in the onion and fresh garlic and cooked until translucent. I added some of the chicken broth and deglazed the pan, throwing it all into the crockpot over the meat. I then added the rest of the broth, and all the veggies except the squash and the apples. I cooked on high for an hour, then turned down to low. After about 4 hours, I added the butternut squash (I didn't want it to get too disintegrated, my crockpot cooks pretty hot). About an hour before it was done, I put in the 2 peeled and sliced apples, and 1/2 cup apple cider. I didn't find that I needed to add any flour or cornstarch, probably because I browned the meat in flour first. This dish smelled amazing

Delicious! I doubled it for big family gathering, put it in 5 qt. pan. Didn't have room to double potatoes and apples, but still great. Everyone loved it and asked for the recipe! I added apple cider in addition to/instead of chicken broth and a few dashes soy sauce. I increased salt a bit, added garlic and onion powders in addition to the fresh garlic & onion. The sage and rosemary really complement this dish well! Make sure you use very fresh spices, as is the case with any recipe. I also used beef chuck roast since I didn't have pork handy and it was awesome. I look forward to trying it with pork. I also used fresh butternut squash, peeled with vegetable peeler and cubed, since that's all I had on hand. Yummers! Oh, and since I like the meat very tender, I simmered the meat with liquids/spices about an hour before adding veggies, then simmered another 1/2 hour. Adding the veggies long after the meat was an excellent idea and helped veggies retain their pretty color and shapes. I cut carrots on the bias for oval shapes instead of cubing, but either would be pretty.

Excellent Stew. I took the advice or a previous reviewer and let the pork cook in the just the liquid portion of the recipe for a little over an hour. This made the pork melt in your mouth tender. I added an extra half cup of water to compensate for the extra cooking. I chopped fresh sage leaves and added a generous portions at least 10 leaves. The taste of the fresh sage and the apples was outstanding. I cooked all the vegetables for 20 min as the recipe calls for. I did however use fresh butternut squash andadded the squash about 15 min before the recipe was done instead of 20 min. I also added a little bit of cornstarch dissolved in cold water to thicken it especially since I added extra water. Instead of putting potatoes in the stew I served it with a side of roasted garlic mashed potatoes. The mashed potatoes complimented the stew as it gave you something to eat the gravy with. I will definitely make this again.

Great recipe! I was searching for a pork stew recipe and found this one. I just happened to have a butternut squash too. I made the recipe pretty much as written, adding salt and pepper to the meat when browning it, added herb de provence instead of rosemary (it is in it). I steamed the potatoes and squash and served them with it. I used Pink Lady apples and put them in 10 minutes before it was done. I added the carrots with the onion and garlic plus added chopped turnip, celery root and parsnip (had a stew mix of veggies at home already). Considered thickening the broth but we decided not to and I am glad it was so lovely. My husband wasn't sure he would like it, but he was pleasantly surprised he said and ate a huge bowl and took a huge box of it to work the next day. Thanks for the lovely recipe.

This recipe turned out so good. Ways I changed it: I used chicken instead of pork. I cooked the chicken, garlic and onions for an hour (instead of 20 minutes) to make sure it was nice and tender. I added about 3x the amount of sage and rosemary. I also added garlic powder. Instead of 2 potatoes, I used one potato and 1 yam. I also added 2 stalks of celery. I used fresh butternut squash, instead of frozen. Added the squash and apples in just the last 5 min. so they were just tender. We loved it!!

I made this last night and it was GREAT! The flavors were so complementary of eachother. I used fresh butternut squash, the potatoes, and carrots for more substance. But because I added the extra veggies, I used 4 cups of chicken broth, otherwise there wouldn't have been enough liquid. I simmered the pork chunks in the flavored broth for about 45 minutes and by the time the soup was done, the meat was so tender! The apples do add a nice unexpected flavor to the soup! I highly recommend making this delicious soup. My meat-and-potatoes husband said that he'd like this one again...and that says alot!

Very tasty dish. I made a few changes that help a lot. First, put the potatoes in when you add the broth instead of in the last step. They need as much time as possible. Second, I browned the meat separately then took it out of the pan and cooked the onions, adding the garlic for the last minute or so before adding them all to the broth. This way, the meat and the garlic don't overcook. I also threw in a little pureed chipotle to give it a little zest. I roasted my own butternut squash to add a depth of flavor from the carmelization. All in all an excellent melding of tastes.

Wonderful flavor and versitility. Great recipe for inexpensive cuts of pork and as long as they are cut into small pieces. Cooks up fast and very tender. Don't leave out the apple at the very end and I added whatever was in the refrigerator. Great way to get the family to eat sweet potatoes, butternut squash and, yes, brussel sprouts. Since I like a thicker stew, added Wondra at the end and seasoned with Kitchen Bouquet for a rich, brown color.

I was leary when I started, but this dish is AWESOME!! As per other reviewers I cooked the pork for 45 minutes for added tenderness Hint: If using fresh butternut squash, wrap it in plastic wrap, jab it with a large meat fork, then nuke it on high for about 5-7 minutes. Let cool a little then cut up. It is much easier to deal with. I also added a few frozen peas at the end just for a little bit more color.

Wow, this is SO unbelievably good! I expected this to be a ho-hum meal, but I had all the ingredients so I was going to make it regardless. I'm so surprised by how incredible this is even with so little spice. The changes I made were: Using pork thigh covered in adobo, subbing stock for water & a bullion cube, & omitting sage (I didn't have any). I also added a sweet potato.

This is seriously one of the best stews I've ever had!
This was delicious. Perfect for a cold winter meal.

Stew with a twist while fulfilling the comfort food on a chilly day. Our friend made this for us during a difficult time. It was comfort food with a twist that made it interesting. I made it today in preparation for the coming artic blast.

We really wanted to like this, but unfortunately, this one just didn't make it in our house. I used the slow cooker method, and included the optional carrots and potatoes. Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly. Despite having lots of good ingredients, the result was disappointing. I'm not sure why, and I'm not sure how it could have been improved. I know I'm in the minority here, but for us, this one isn't a keeper.
Loved this & so did everyone else!
Delicious

This is my 4th time making this and it has become a family favorite! I do use frozen squash as it was easier to find the first time I made it and have found it much easier to use. The first time I made this, I was looking for recipes to use a smoked pork roast I had smoked the day before. I cubed it, and it was spectacular in this stew! The 2nd time I made it I used fresh pork and we all liked it best with the smoked pork roast! So, last night while smoking baby back ribs for dinner, I went ahead and smoked another pork roast and am heading into the kitchen to prepare this wonderful recipe again! THANK YOU!!
Had little to no flavor. I was very disappointed. Then I added a lot more spices, some mushrooms, celery and spinach, and it was edible the next day. I was so disappointed.

I made this for dinner tonight and it was delicious! I pretty much followed the recipe. I just added a little extra potato and squash because I like it. A couple reviews said it was a tad bland, so in addition to the spices it called for, I threw in a couple pinches of Allspice as well. It was the perfect comfort soup for cold dreary weather with just a hint of sweetness. If I could give it more stars, I would! ??

No changes and once it was made I canned it up for the winter.

Excellent
